# pixdial

> Live hardware readings on Lian Li UNI FAN SL Wireless LCD (SL V3) fans on Linux, with a
> Python SDK and CLI. Free software under GPL-3.0-or-later.

pixdial draws live hardware readings on round LCD panels. It includes 14 designs,
three themes (warm, ember and ice), and Python plugins for designs, sources and devices.
Supported panels, both round 400 × 400 pixels, on Linux:

- Lian Li UNI FAN SL Wireless LCD (SL V3), USB 1cbe:0005: tested
- Lian Li UNI FAN TL Wireless LCD (TL V2), USB 1cbe:0006: experimental, same protocol

Each LCD needs its own USB cable to a USB 2 header. pixdial draws the screens only:
it does not control fan speed or RGB lighting.

Requires Python 3.12+ and uv (or pipx). Install from PyPI:

    uv tool install pixdial

`pixdial render crown --out preview` produces a demo PNG without hardware,
including on macOS. Website images show demo readings. PSU readings, connector
currents and agent quota require configured sources.

Built-in sensor readers use local files or NVML. No telemetry or network service.
Configured commands and plugins can use the network and run with the user's permissions.

The SL V3 protocol follows sgtaziz/lian-li-linux v1.2.6 (Copyright (c) 2026 sgtaziz, MIT).
lian-li-linux is a Linux replacement for L-Connect 3: fan speed, pumps, RGB lighting and
LCDs with images, GIFs, video, sensor presets, templates and a template editor. The two
run side by side: lian-li-linux keeps fans and RGB, and pixdial draws the LCDs once they
are out of lian-li-linux's LCD list. pixdial is not affiliated with Lian Li.
